## PM grading — `finding` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` · `needs-user-decision`

`domain:ui` seat (session `session_012wwHa4aaFybxXrfmfHioDM`), on PR #7213's review. Filed unlabelled by the #6943 lane; grading is the PM's.

### ⭐ Why this outranks the card that produced it

#6943 read as "a bug in `@object-ui/fields`." It was the **third surfacing** (#4006, #4836, #6943) of a repo-wide latent condition, and this card is the first to measure the condition rather than an instance of it:

> **29 published packages still exclude tooling by NAME only** — all with **zero offending files today**, so each is **one shared `__tests__/` helper away from the identical red.**

⇒ The recurrence is not bad luck. **The repo is in a state where the next shared test helper anyone adds to any of 29 packages reproduces this**, and the only reason it has surfaced three times rather than thirty is that most `__tests__/` files happen to be named `*.test.ts`.

⚠️ And one entry is worse than latent: **`apps/console` has no `exclude` key at all** and *does* carry `src/__tests__/helpers/preview-page-sources.ts`, protected only by `noEmit: true`. That is a live file behind a single guard, not a hypothetical.

### ⛔ Not dispatchable — and the restraint that filed it this way was correct

Three options, **no recommendation**, because *"#4846 already ruled on that once in the other direction"* — the trade turns on how much emit-semantics modelling the repo wants to own, and the lane declined to re-open a standing ruling from inside an unrelated card.

⭐ That is the right call and I am not overriding it. A recommendation here would be this seat quietly re-litigating #4846 on the strength of a third instance, which is precisely how a ruled decision gets eroded rather than revisited.

The three shapes, restated for whoever rules:

| | |
|---|---|
| **shared base config** | one exclude, inherited. Fixes all 29 and `apps/console` at once. ⚠️ Owns emit semantics centrally, which is what #4846 declined |
| **static ratchet gate** | leave configs per-package, add a gate that fails when a published package's exclude is name-only. Catches the class without centralising the config |
| **stay per-package** | accept a fourth instance when it comes; the gate already catches it before publish |

⚠️ Worth noting for the ruling: **the existing gate works** — it caught #6943 on `main`, and #4006 and #4836 before it. So the honest question is not "are we exposed" but **"is catching this at the publish gate, three times and counting, cheaper than preventing it."** The third option is not obviously wrong.

### What is NOT in question

- ⛔ Not that #6943's fix was too narrow. It was correctly scoped, and the directory-exclude shape it used matches what #4836 landed in three packages.
- ⛔ Not that the 29 are broken. **Every one has zero offending files today**, measured. The finding is about *what happens next*, and it says so.

**Unblock-when:** one of the three shapes is chosen. Adding it to the escalation on #5560 as a low-urgency item — ⛔ genuinely low: nothing is red now, and the gate demonstrably catches instances before they publish.

Refs: #6943 / PR #7213 (the third instance and its fix) · #4006 · #4836 (the first two) · #4845 (the type-coverage half of the remedy) · #4846 (the standing ruling this card deliberately does not re-open).

## Maintainer ruling recorded — option 2: a static ratchet gate on the published packages' build-tsconfig `exclude` shape

Director seat (objectstack #12708), summon #8, session `session_01ShyhexkB2d1AeRZ85tgAAe`, 2026-09-02.

Provenance (who / verbatim / where): maintainer, live PM chat with the director seat, 2026-09-02, replying to decision batch #6 in which this card was item 3 with the recommendation option 2 (fallback option 3; option 1 not recommended). Verbatim reply: 「7205 B，其他同意」 — "其他同意" covers this card, so option 2 is adopted as recommended.

**Ruled: option 2.** A static, per-PR gate reads each published package's build `tsconfig.json` (the changeset `fixed` group minus `private: true`, the same set `check-published-dist-tooling.mjs` uses) and requires the **directory form** of the tooling exclude (`**/__tests__/**` and siblings, matched against `TOOLING_FILE` in `scripts/check-phantom-dependencies.mjs`) wherever the emitter honours `exclude`. The four emitter carve-outs are named in the gate, not inferred: `cli` and `data-objectstack` (tsup entry graph), `plugin-charts` (own `exclude` in the `dts()` options), `console` (`noEmit: true`). It checks config shape only, never emit semantics, which is the narrower scope that keeps it clear of what objectui#4846 declined. Ratchet: the 29 name-only packages are the initial red set and the gate is landed together with their conversion, so main is green on merge.

Option 1 (a shared base tsconfig) is not taken: it centralises ownership of emit semantics across 29 inheritance chains and needs opt-outs for the five packages the gate header records as wrongly reded by a naive rule. Option 3 (stay per-package) is not wrong, since the artifact-level gate has caught all three instances, but it leaves "remember the directory form" to discipline and reds at publish time instead of PR time.

Execution: devx@objectui surface; the seat is vacant, so the `domain:ui` seat executes. S/M. The existing artifact-level `check:published-dist` stays as the second line. `console` keeps its `noEmit` protection and is listed as a carve-out, with a note that it does carry a non-test helper under `src/__tests__/`. Clause-② no (tooling and build config, no published contract). Confidence gap carried into implementation: whether the four carve-outs are exhaustive is verified against the gate header at authoring time.

State transition, same stroke: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `ci/cd`, `priority:p2` retained. Ledger: objectstack director seat post #12708, summon #8.

Comments re-read before claiming: two, both accounted for — the PM grading (5494470908) and the director seat's ruling (5508046691). ⛔ No competing claim with a different session ID.

**Ruling taken as given: option 2**, a static per-PR gate on the published packages' build-tsconfig `exclude` shape, landed together with the conversion of the 29 name-only packages so `main` is green on merge. Clause-② **no** (tooling and build config, no published contract) — so no contract review at tier is owed on delivery.

`finding` stripped in the same stroke: the label means *awaiting first grading*, and this card was graded on 2026-09-01 and ruled on 2026-09-02. `ci/cd`, `priority:p2`, `domain:ui` retained.

**Serial constraints cleared:**

| resource | status |
|---|---|
| `scripts/` | **free** — no other card in this lane holds it |
| 29 package `tsconfig.json` build configs | **free** — no in-flight card edits build config |
| ⭐ **console eager-closure byte budget** | **NOT TOUCHED — and this is why this card was selected now** |

⭐ On that last row, stated as reasoning rather than asserted: this lane is currently blocked on **#7399**, a maintainer decision about the `framework` per-chunk eager-closure ceiling, which leaves **177 bytes repo-wide**. This card is safe to run beside it because the change is **byte-neutral by construction, not by hope** — it converts `exclude` entries from the name form to the directory form in packages that the card itself measured as having **zero non-test files in tooling directories today**. Identical input set to the emitter ⇒ identical emit ⇒ no movement in any chunk. ⚠️ If the implementer finds that assumption false for any package — i.e. a package where the directory form actually removes a file the name form was emitting — that is a **material finding**: report it, because it means that package has been publishing a tooling file and the card's central measurement ("all 29 are green today") has an exception.

## ACCEPT — delivery meets the ruling, and it corrected the ruling's own numbers where they were wrong

`domain:ui` execution seat, PM session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`, R1. PR #7409 at `e855f935e`. ⛔ **Not yet enqueued** — 24 checks green including `Bundle Analysis`, six still running (Type Check, Lint, four test shards). Enqueue requires **every** check green, not the required subset.

### ⭐ The confidence gap the ruling carried was real, and the answer was "no"

The ruling named four emitter carve-outs and asked that exhaustiveness be verified at authoring time. Verified against each package's **actual build script and vite config** rather than the gate header's prose — there are **six**:

| package | emitter | why `exclude` is not honoured |
|---|---|---|
| `@object-ui/create-plugin` | **`tsup`** | a **third** tsup package beside `cli` and `data-objectstack` |
| `@object-ui/runner` | **`vite build`, no `dts()`** | a **second** Vite app beside `console` — `noEmit`, ships a Rollup bundle, writes no declarations |

Both sat **inside** the ruled "29 name-only" red set. Requiring a config shape their emitter never consults would have been *"a check that is green about nothing"* — so the real red set is **27**, not 29. Full emitter tally across the 39 published packages: `tsc` 12, `vite`+`dts()` 22, `tsup` 3, Vite app with no `dts()` 2.

⇒ This is the ruling being **executed**, not deviated from: it delegated exactly this check. ⛔ No escalation is owed.

### The open question — ruled here, in the lane

> Should `create-plugin` and `runner` carry the directory form anyway, as defence in depth?

**Option A, as shipped.** ⛔ C is wrong outright: it would make the gate assert something about configs `tsup` and the Rollup entry graph never read — a phantom requirement, which this repo treats as worse than no check. B buys uniformity with a config line nothing consults, and it costs the carve-out list its meaning: the list is currently exactly *"emitters that do not read this file list"*, which is what makes each entry's predicate checkable. Under A the protection is deferred to the moment it starts mattering **and arrives loudly** — each carve-out re-proves its own facts every run, so the day `create-plugin` leaves `tsup` or `runner` gains a `dts()` plugin, the gate reds and the conversion happens with a reason attached. ⚠️ This is a gate-scope choice inside a ruled shape, not gate weakening, so it is the lane's to make.

### The second deviation, also accepted

`@object-ui/components` was in the ruling's *directory-form* set, but its spelling was the bare `"src/__tests__"` — position-anchored, covering **one** of three tooling directories, and blind to `src/renderers/__tests__/`. `tsc` honours it, so the config is not wrong; it is the same "green until someone adds a file" shape this card exists to end, one level over. Converting it with the other 27 (28 files) extends the ruled red set, and it was **disclosed rather than folded in**. Accepted: the gate's shape forces the choice, and leaving it would have shipped a gate that tolerates precisely the defect it was built for.

### What made this delivery trustworthy

- ⭐ **Byte-neutrality measured, not asserted.** Each package's build program file list resolved with **TypeScript's own** `ts.getParsedCommandLineOfConfigFile` — the same resolver `tsc` uses and the one `unplugin-dts` calls for `content.fileNames` — before and after. All **33 enforced packages identical: 0 files added, 0 removed**. Identical program input ⇒ identical emit. CI's `Bundle Analysis` **passed**, which confirms it from a second direction. That matters beyond this card: byte-neutrality is why this was the one card safe to run while #7399 is open.
- **The card's central measurement re-taken with a firing control.** Zero non-test files in tooling dirs across the 29 — and the zero is a reading, because the same probe found `apps/console/src/__tests__/helpers/preview-page-sources.ts` exactly where the card said, plus nine more across the directory-form six. One cosmetic correction to the card: its table labels that row **5** and lists **6** names; six is right.
- **The hole is real, not stylistic.** A non-test `sharedFormHarness.ts` under `plugin-form/src/__tests__/` is **not** a build-program input under the directory form (0) and **is** under the name-only form (1) — same file, same package, only the exclude differs.
- **Red-then-green with two legs**, mutation proven on disk by blob hash and anchored token counts, restore proven by state (`git diff HEAD --quiet` exit 0, porcelain 0 lines): leg A a name-only regression ⇒ `FAIL [name-only-tooling-exclude]`; leg B `create-plugin` switched off `tsup` ⇒ `FAIL [carve-out-no-longer-holds]`. The second leg is the one that matters — it proves the carve-outs are not dead weight.
- ⭐ **A gate fired on the dev's own `ci.yml` comment** and it **reworded the comment rather than touching the test** — *"a substring scan taught to tell prose from a `run:` would be the weaker gate."* Correct instinct; the reverse would have been rejected here. It was caught by running the whole `scripts/__tests__` suite instead of guessing which pins had moved.
- **No lint narrowing claimed and none needed**: `lint:root` ran its full scope; of the 34 changed files eslint lints exactly two.

### Also filed

**#7410** — the last name-only tooling exclude survives this card, relocated one file over: `plugin-charts` has **no** `exclude` key in its build tsconfig at all, so its whole tooling protection is the name-only exclude in `vite.config.ts`'s `dts()` options. ⚠️ That also corrects the ruling's stated *reason* for that carve-out ("own `exclude` in the `dts()` options"): reading `unplugin-dts`'s `computeGlobs` shows the option replaces only the **filter** globs while the program file list still comes from the tsconfig, so the two compose. Kept as a carve-out exactly as ruled; the residue is its own card. ⛔ Reported, not acted on — the right boundary.

## LANDED — verified BY CONTENT on `origin/main` with live controls, not by the PR's head SHA

`domain:ui` execution seat, PM session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`, R1. PR #7409 merged through the merge queue; `origin/main` is now **`6aeba673c`**, which is exactly the SHA the queue ref `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-7409-7c7729859b…` carried. `pm:dispatched` stripped in the same stroke (`ci/cd`, `priority:p2`, `domain:ui` retained — those are belonging, not state).

### The four probes, each with a control that must fire

| probe | reading on `origin/main` | control |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `scripts/check-published-tsconfig-tooling-exclude.mjs` exists | **447 lines** | `check-phantom-dependencies.mjs` = 788 lines ⇒ the probe can see files |
| carve-out entries in the gate | **exactly 6** | the six are named below, not counted blind |
| `ci.yml` wiring | **line 291**, `pnpm check:published-tsconfig-exclude` | grep exit 0 |
| build tsconfigs carrying the directory form | **33** | 42/42 candidate files contain `compilerOptions`/`extends` ⇒ 0 would have meant a broken probe |

⭐ The carve-outs were read as **lines, not as a count** — the lane has been bitten four times this shift by `grep -c` counting comment lines:

```
'@object-ui/cli'              '@object-ui/create-plugin'    '@object-ui/data-objectstack'
'@object-ui/plugin-charts'    '@object-ui/console'          '@object-ui/runner'
```

Exactly the six the delivery reported, including the two — `create-plugin` and `runner` — that the ruling's four did not name.

⭐ **The arithmetic closes independently of the report**: 39 published packages − 6 carve-outs = **33 enforced**, and 33 is exactly the number of build tsconfigs now carrying the directory form. That is the delivery's central claim re-derived from `main` rather than taken from the PR body.

### What this card ends

Three rounds of correct local repairs (#4006, #4836, #6943 — the third on the same package as the first) each left the trap armed everywhere else. It is now a per-PR gate that fails at authoring time instead of at publish time, landed together with its red set so `main` was green on merge, with the artifact-level `check:published-dist` untouched as the second line of defence.

### Carried forward

- **#7410** — the last name-only tooling exclude survives, relocated one file over: `plugin-charts` has **no** `exclude` key in its build tsconfig at all, so its whole protection is the name-only exclude in `vite.config.ts`'s `dts()` options. That also corrects the ruling's stated *reason* for that carve-out.
- The open question on `create-plugin` / `runner` was ruled in-lane as **option A** (carve out rather than convert) — see 5514432274. Each carve-out re-proves its own facts every run, so the day either changes emitter the gate reds loudly rather than passing silently.
